newsitem.title: BRAZIL: BRAZIL OFFERS CHEAP FINANCE FOR TELECOM INVESTMENT.
newsitem.headline: BRAZIL OFFERS CHEAP FINANCE FOR TELECOM INVESTMENT.

text.p: The Brazilian government is offering cheap finance to investors in cellular Band B infrastructure and equipment and plans to extend the scheme to fixed-line telecommunications investment, officials said.

Luiz Carlos Mendonca de Barros, head of the National Development Bank (BNDES), said the cheap credit lines would not only encourage rapid and large investment in the sector, but also help slow the expansion of Brazil's trade deficit.
Overseas investors should not just eye Brazil because of its large domestic market, but also as an exporting base for the Mercosur trade bloc and the rest of Latin America.
Communications Minister Sergio Motta said no specific limit was set on the funds dedicated to the financing plan.
"The resources will be determined by market demand," Motta said at a news conference held with Mendonca de Barros.
In a statement, the BNDES said it would finance up to 100 percent of the value of infrastructure investment carried out by operators of Band B concessions.
It said it would finance up to 100 percent of factory installation costs for telecommunications equipment makers and 80 percent of the plant installation costs of component manufacturers.

The finance will have a 10-year maturity and a 36-month grace period. Beneficiaries will pay the BNDES its normal long-term interest rate plus one percentage point a year and a spread for risk, which will depend on individual analyses.
Mendonca de Barros said the BNDES planned to extend the credit to fixed-line infrastructure once consultants start putting together the sale plan for state holding Telebras at the end of October.
He said the bank was also participating through risk capital investment in consortia bidding to run band B cellular telephone services.
The BNDES will be limited to 19.9 percent of the social capital of any venture, or 200 million reais.
